Quantum tunneling is an inherent process that lacks a direct analogy in classical physics, and it can rival Coulomb interactions to give rise to non-trivial phenomena.
In silicon, precise placement of phosphorus dopants is feasible to address the diverse consequences of tunneling, thereby exploiting this means of coupling to drive quantum applications and studies.
By employing a minimal model that accounts for orbital and spin degrees of freedom, the present work delves into the impact of tunneling on paired dopants in silicon using a perturbative approach.
Tunneling-induced couplings between qubits via a common orbital are investigated, and the findings are consistent with prior experiments using NMR.
Moreover, the research demonstrates that tunneling can induce complex Heisenberg interactions between spin-functional groups without requiring a common mediator, a phenomenon that may be verifiable using silicon qubit technologies.
Finally, the study examines how tunneling affects the energy levels of paired qubits and reveals that their ground states can be coupled even in the absence of Coulomb interaction, paving the way for the development of entangled quantum states and their application in creating magnetic-symmetrical structures.

Several disciplines have been influenced by optimization techniques in various real-world scenarios. As a result of ongoing research into a wide array of optimization methods within the operations research and management science fields, there's a growing need within academic and professional settings to efficiently compare and replicate these studies. To address this challenge, the Open Source Optimization framework, specifically libOPT, offers a versatile tool for seamlessly integrating and testing optimization techniques. With the aim of enhancing its user-friendly features, libOPT has been revamped to incorporate a range of user-friendly attributes, essentially transforming it into a comprehensive optimization software library. This paper outlines the enhancements to libOPT, focusing on the implementation of its non-linear programming capabilities via the reduced basis approach, in addition to enhancing its efficiency through multi-threading operations. A significant advancement involves the incorporation of a dynamic scheduling policy designed to accelerate solution times, particularly for optimization problems with intricate constraints.

Given an algebraic variety X that has a transitive action from the group Aut(X), the highest degree of transitivity of this action is called the transitivity degree. This degree is denoted by the maximum value of m for which Aut(X) acts transitively m times on X. In cases where Aut(X) is m-transitive for any positive value of m, we define the transitivity degree to be infinite. This study involves determining the transitivity degree for specific varieties, such as quasi-affine toric varieties, and homogeneous spaces, while exploring related open problems and conjectures.

In non-commutative space-time deformations, the definition of identical particles breaks down. These models are described by non-abelian space symmetries represented by a four-momentum group. Our approach recognizes that for multi-particle states, the total system momentum is the only well-defined property. Calculating the total momentum involves non-commutative composition of individual particle momenta, which become ambiguous. Our results indicate that previous Fock space constructions were flawed due to incorrect assumptions and lack success. We demonstrate that momentum exchange underlies a potential route to constructing a fully canonical quantum field theory in these space deformations.

We apply the two-photon absorption transient current technique to study
properties of wide bandgap semiconductors. We utilize this technique to
investigate charge transport in scCVD diamond by exciting its charge carriers
with a femtosecond laser. Due to its two-photon nature, the technique confines
charge carrier generation in 3-D around the laser focal point. This localized
charge injection enables us to study the semiconductor bulk with high 3-D
resolution. We mapped the diamond's bulk electrical field at varying depths by
taking advantage of charge spatial confinement. The results were then compared
to X-ray diffraction topography. The approach allows for unique insights into
charge transport in transparent wide bandgap materials.

Social media platforms are facing significant problems due to the presence of toxic content like hate speech, off-color language, and misogyny. These difficulties have caught the attention of the Natural Language Processing (NLP) community, driving innovative research in the field. In this study, we report on the performance of our models in the inaugural Arabic Misogyny Identification challenge, where we evaluate three models that can learn multiple tasks simultaneously, alongside their individual-task counterparts. Our approach relies on the pre-trained MARBERT language model to analyze text inputs. Our results indicate that the proposed models achieved top-tier outcomes, securing first, second, and third place in both the misogyny identification and classification tasks.

This study centres around the solvability of a distinct class of fractional backward stochastic differential equations that take into account past influences within their generators, under Lipschitz condition it's demonstrated that the existence and uniqueness of such equations are assured. Furthermore, a key comparison theorem has been formulated.

We examine if controllers obtained using model-based Reinforcement Learning, which employs an environment model to find the optimal policy, maintain their effectiveness in dynamic scenarios. Building upon the work of Poupart and Courtemanche (2005), we discover that integrating the Koopman operator theory into these models yields conditions under which they become invariant in dynamic contexts, enabling them to adapt naturally to changing conditions. This leads to a straightforward algorithm that updates the environment model when internal state variations are detected. Empirical testing conducted on multiple continuous control domains verifies the validity of our proposed approach.

Several key network communication challenges such as caching and computation are interconnected. A centralized caching approach seeks to mitigate network strain during peak wireless network times, whereas distributed computation explores the potential for processing data at the edge of the network. Despite their significance, caching and computation are complicated by the limitations of separate and overlapping strategies. In this paper, an integrated framework for caching and computation is proposed, enabling fundamental bounds on caching and computation capacities to be interlinked. The framework's relevance is demonstrated through new, separately optimal caching and computation schemes in various network settings, including a comprehensive expression for the caching capacity of a wireless network with a single gateway and separate expression for the computation capacity of a wireless network with a single gateway and multiple sources. The framework's flexibility is illustrated through general, separable expressions for caching and computation capacities in networks with multiple sources and destinations. In addition, new, separate bounds on caching and computation capacities are provided for general network configurations with multiple sources and destinations.

We establish a formalization of the Scott model in uncurried PCF, with the aim of comparing it to the LOPM and LOPM$_\tau$ models. To do this, we derive an explicit description for the lifting monad in PCF in terms of Scott domains, leveraging recent advances in category theory. Furthermore, we observe that any program in PCF can be transformed into an equivalent partial function on the natural numbers, with the addition of a single 'lift' instruction.

Hanzer and Muić's work on degenerate Eisenstein series cancellations has been built upon, 
extending their method and outcome to a specific set of Eisenstein series, 
specifically those formed from the combinations of two Speh representations 
$\Delta(\tau,m)|\cdot|^{s_1}\otimes\Delta(\tau,n)|\cdot|^{s_2}$ in $GL(m+n,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$ for self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation $\tau$.

Designing effective collision avoidance systems for mobile robots remains a key challenge, particularly when accounting for the robot's spatial structure.
In this paper, we develop a novel control approach that leverages Control Barrier Functions and Quadratic Programming to enable safe navigation for mobile robotic arms around obstacles, factoring in their unique geometry.
Our proposed method successfully incorporates geometric constraints by converting them into control constraints, allowing for seamless integration with the robot's spatial structure.
Simulation results confirm that our method enables safe and efficient navigation for both simple and complex robotic arms.
Furthermore, we demonstrate that our method can be scaled to handle multiple moving obstacles through a significant number of test scenarios.

Natural language processing, a crucial field of study, strives to comprehend text via digital analysis, despite the inherent imperfections arising from diverse forms of written and spoken language. This work delves into employing various graph-based methodologies for resolving the challenge of text summarization via a selective extraction technique. Two key indicators – sentence overlap and edit distance – are employed for gauging sentence similarity.

Researchers have suggested the application of quantum interferometry and information processing in Bose-Einstein condensates. However, the current understanding of BECs relies on classical descriptions, which do not adequately describe the behavior of low-temperature condensates. Our work develops a quantum mechanics framework for BECs, which enables the description of nonlinear systems through solution of the time-dependent Schrodinger equation. In contrast to classical descriptions, our approach reveals the emergence of shock waves and other singular behaviors, which can be harnessed for quantum interferometry and information processing. Our findings open the door for quantum utilities by demonstrating that nonlinear interactions can produce coherent states, as well as other exotic phenomena. To facilitate practical applications, we also explore methods for controlling and manipulating coherent states, which could be achieved through coherent pulse sequences. Furthermore, the possibility of combining multiple paths and systems leads to the notion of composite nonlinear quantum systems, which can be used to construct and control large, complex structures. These extensions of traditional quantum systems hold immense potential for innovative research in quantum physics.

This paper aims to accomplish two distinct objectives. Firstly, it seeks to establish a unicity theorem for meromorphic mappings from a complete Kähler manifold to a complex projective space, under the constraint of limited intersection with hypersurfaces. Secondly, the paper aims to prove a unicity theorem for the case of nondegenerate meromorphic mappings that share a specified number of hyperplanes in a particular geometric configuration.

Polynomial system solving plays a crucial role in various applications to capture nonlinear geometric attributes. To obtain a solution set devoid of degeneration, which end-users seek to avoid, the nondegenerate locus of a polynomial system needs to be computed. The nondegenerate locus comprises points where the codimension of the solution set matches the number of equations in the system. Historically, the nondegenerate locus has been obtained using ideal-theoretic techniques like saturation ideals and equidimensional ideals, which prove useful in codimension one situations. However, these methods have inherent shortcomings: they fail to provide results for higher codimensions and make it difficult to integrate other algorithms due to the introduction of irrelevant equations through equidimensional decomposition. To overcome these limitations and offer more flexibility, we propose an operator-based approach to calculate the nondegenerate locus directly from the polynomial system without the need for intermediate simplifications. By applying this approach, various techniques like operator-based FGLM reduction can be integrated at any stage of the computation.

Direct photons have been measured at $p_T<5$ GeV/$c$ for midrapidity and most central events of Cu$+$Cu collisions at $\sqrt{s_{_{NN}}}=200$ GeV. By calculating the $e^{+}e^{-}$ excess in the $e^{+}e^{-}$ mass distribution over hadronic contributions, we found that quasi-real direct virtual photons significantly contribute to the photon spectrum. In Cu$+$Cu collisions, photons show a higher production rate than what would be expected from scaling p+$p$ collisions based on the number of binary collisions. This phenomenon persists across various centrality intervals. Furthermore, we found that the photon spectrum in Cu$+$Cu collisions has a similar transverse momentum shape to that measured in p+$p$ collisions but has a higher yield than what is observed in p+$p$ events at the same $\sqrt{s}$, after accounting for binary scaling.

The Turan tetrahedron problem seeks to calculate the Turan density of the tetrahedron graph K4^3 by finding the maximum l1-norm of a K4^3-free n-vertex 3-uniform hypergraph exponent, where n increases proportionally to the vertices of K4^3. Our study focuses on determining an upper bound for this exponent and we define a hypergraph property 'f' as follows: for every given e1, e2, and e3, where the sum of their codegrades is 3, and given a set V of n vertices, where the codegrades of e1, e2, and e3 lie within it, the subgraph 3-uniform hypergraph induced by V contains either an e1-e2-e3-hyperpath or an e1-e2-hyperpath or an e1-e3-hyperpath or an e2-e3-hyperpath. We show that a K4^3-free n-vertex 3-uniform hypergraph of property 'f' exists and deduce the quadruplet sum property for such a hypergraph: for every given e1, e2, e3, and e4, where the sum of their codegrades is 4, and given a set V of n vertices, where the codegrades of e1, e2, e3, and e4 lie within it, the subgraph 3-uniform hypergraph induced by

Achieving a proper balance between visual quality and performance is a prime consideration in rendering vector maps. A well-placed level of spatial anti-aliasing can enhance visual appearance, but may also compromise system efficiency. The impact of anti-aliasing, when combined with vector map topology changes, has yet to be systematically investigated. This study offers insights into the effects of spatial anti-aliasing on visual experience and system performance in the context of varying vector map topologies. Our findings serve as a foundation for an algorithm developed to regulate anti-aliasing levels according to the intricate structure of the rendered area. The proposed method is informed by these findings and effectively manages anti-aliasing to achieve the optimal rendering balance between visual quality and system performance.

The multivariate interpolation operator is traditionally constructed using piecewise linear functions to approximate absolute differences between values. In this study, we develop a novel, transcendental interpolation function derived from the hyperbolic tangent, providing more precise approximations of functions that increase linearly with the distance. Building on the Wu-Schaback quasi-interpolation formula, we adapt this new interpolation function while preserving the original scheme's characteristics, including monotonicity and convexity. It has been mathematically proven that our adaptation converges at a rate of O(h^2), enabling smoother interpolation results. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this new technique achieves greater precision than the traditional multiquadric method, also providing an efficient implementation that surpasses its performance.

Pulsar halos are large-scale, high-energy emission structures, formed when energetic electrons and positrons break free from pulsar wind nebulae. As a novel category of gamma-ray emitters, pulsar halos serve as optimal probes for examining the diffusion of cosmic rays within the Galaxy's localized areas, as well as their escape from pulsar wind nebulae. Research on pulsar halos has brought to light that their associated diffusion coefficient is substantially lower than the overall average in the Galaxy, thus generating considerable interest among scientists. We delve into the recent breakthroughs regarding pulsar halos, including their identification methods, energy spectrum, spatial distribution, spectral connections with parent pulsar wind nebulae, and the underlying implications for the investigation of cosmic-ray propagation in the Galaxy.

Transportation systems are frequently hindered by unpredictable weather conditions.
Current methods of weather prediction, using either a network of sensors or a vehicle-mounted camera, are limited in scope and costly.
A robust weather detection system is crucial for seamless operation of transportation services in diverse weather conditions.
However, this task is complex due to the varied nature of weather and the scarcity of distinct characteristics that distinguish different weather conditions.
Existing approaches to this problem are largely confined to specific environments and only tackle the classification of two weather types.
In this study, we introduce the RFS dataset, which includes images representing three categories of weather (rain, snow, and fog), and propose a novel algorithm utilizing super-pixel masks for data augmentation to yield satisfactory results using multiple Convolutional Neural Networks.

Our analysis examines how climate change interest shifts among diverse groups and how their individual interests interconnect. Initially, we track the individual trends, followed by developing a cross-influence model that we then validate using Acorn news data. Our results indicate significant fluctuations in the general public's climate change interest, as well as notable cross-effects between the media and the general public.

Soft grippers are increasingly popular across various applications due to their versatility and flexibility, yet accurately modeling and controlling them to grasp objects efficiently remains challenging. Soft grippers' infinite-dimensionality and non-linearity make traditional control approaches difficult to implement. In response, researchers have turned to data-driven methods. However, current methods typically require extensive model learning through simulations or offline processes, which often fails to adapt to novel scenarios or real-time physical robot control requirements. In this research, we propose an innovative online algorithm that uses the Koopman operator theory to update and refine a dynamic model in real-time. By integrating the updated model into a Model Predictive Control (MPC) structure, our approach enables successful deployment on physical robots without the need for extensive simulation or offline preparation. Our proposed method has been validated through experiments in multiple domains, including a specific test case of grasping objects in a real-world scenario.

One of the fundamental problems in science and engineering involves finding the lowest cost value for a given function, known as an optimization problem. Various numerical methods have been proposed to solve this problem, but the Gradient Descent method remains the most popular due to its ease and effectiveness. Nonetheless, this approach faces challenges with local minima and slow convergence, particularly when near the optimal point. In response, researchers developed the Natural Gradient Descent method to improve performance across multiple domains, including machine learning, tensor networks, and quantum algorithms. Our work presents a new method to further expand upon NGD, utilizing a suitable reference manifold to expedite convergence and enhance understanding of optimization methods.

High-energy emissions from ancient supermassive black holes can provide a direct look into the black hole activity in the early universe. Specifically, misaligned jets of high-redshift active galaxies should make up a significant portion of these distant galaxy populations. This study uses a highly detailed analysis of data collected from multiple observations of a particularly old and distant galaxy called MS0782+0739. High-resolution imaging of this galaxy's activity allows us to determine the movement of jets over time and identifies distinctive jet alignments, implying that this galaxy is likely a newly formed, dense structure. This discovery is further supported by the detection of a highly unusual, flat spectrum emission coming from the same direction as one of the jets. Using various modeling techniques based on different assumptions about the universe's properties, our research finds that this galaxy is most accurately placed at a distance of around 7.8 billion light-years, with an estimated age of less than 630 million years. Notably, its location is consistent with other similar findings. While its age could be as high as 1.1 billion years, its density and emission patterns suggest that it is likely a compact symmetric object with two lobes separated by about 70 parsecs. This is one of the closest such dense structures to their center, and it is significantly smaller and closer to its center than most similar dense structures. Imaging of its central region reveals a highly unusual ring of light, which is thought to be the result of the accumulation of particles from the jet

This research focuses on improving survival time prediction for lung cancer patients, moving beyond individual clinical indicators to incorporate scan images and text-based clinical data. By merging these diverse data sources, our model generates a unified representation of lung cancer multimodal data. Built on the basis of pre-trained transformers like RoBERTa and ViLT, our proposed model efficiently combines text and image features using a cross-attention mechanism and self-attention technique. Our experiments demonstrate that this model delivers significantly enhanced accuracy in survival time prediction, surpassing existing single-modal approaches.

A well-designed state representation is crucial in the learning process of Reinforcement Learning. Natural language can be utilized in numerous tasks to either represent the state or constitute it entirely. This overview focuses on the techniques employed by researchers to create natural language state representations, underscoring the need for more transparent and contextualized models, thorough justification of design choices and assessments of the relative effectiveness of varying methodologies.

A novel approach combining machine learning is introduced, enabling the accurate reconstruction of high-redshift cosmological density perturbations through observed quasar spectra analysis. By leveraging sophisticated simulations of cosmic structure formation, a substantial synthetic dataset of absorption spectra and associated 1D matter densities is generated. With this dataset, a series of machine learning models are constructed to predict matter density power spectra. We achieve reconstruction accuracy across different scales ($k$) of about 1 percent from the $10^{-4}$ to $10^{-1}$ Hubble volumes, and our results demonstrate potential applications in ongoing and future cosmological surveys, yielding a $4\%$ error in the cosmological parameter $S_8$ when using just the volume out to $k_{max}=0.1$ Hubble inverse lengths.

This paper examines certain types of non-weight modules connected to Lie algebras of the Weyl type. Firstly, we establish the characteristics of modules whose restrictions to $U(\frak h)$ are one-dimensional over Lie algebras representing differential operators on a circle. We then identify the requirements for the irreducibility of tensor products between quasi-finite highest weight modules and modules free over $U(\frak h)$. Additionally, we show that these tensor products are isomorphic only if their corresponding base modules are equivalent, before expanding our findings to cover general Lie algebras representing differential operators.

Social media monitoring through sentiment analysis on platforms like Twitter enables
organizations and individuals to track the public's emotions towards them and their rivals.
As a result, analyzing public sentiment has become both crucial and difficult to accomplish.
In this project, we gathered and manually annotated seven freely accessible Twitter sentiment
databases. We then compiled a new set of training and testing data from these sources. An
LSTM-based classification model was developed to determine the sentiment expressed in
individual tweets. The model's performance was assessed using the newly created dataset.

Recent advances in open-domain dialogue models have achieved significant breakthroughs.
Despite this, developing a scalable chat system poses a major challenge due to
the requirement for substantial human-human dialogue data to support features
like persona, style, or safety. To tackle this issue, our work aims to introduce
role constraints to open-domain dialogue systems that enable them to consistently
maintain assigned roles during human conversations. Achieving this involves
defining a role specification with specific criteria for stated features and
policies on allowed types of utterances. To build this system efficiently, we
propose a framework for collecting data that leverages few-shot learning from
large language models, thereby enabling the creation of role-compliant dialogue
datasets from scratch. Furthermore, we examine various open-domain dialogue
system architectures in terms of their ability to meet role specifications and
maintain natural conversation. Results from both automatic and human evaluations
reveal that our models perform satisfactorily in terms of role conformance, while
still delivering competitive performance on overall conversational metrics.

The binary black hole merger's aftermath leaves a lasting mark on the spacetime, known as gravitational wave memory. Multiple events create a background of residual gravitational waves that can be modeled as stationary stochastic processes. This paper focuses on the power spectral density (PSD) of the gravitational wave memory background, confirming an earlier prediction that its PSD declines at a frequency inverse proportional to the square of the frequency. Building on this finding, the paper makes a new prediction that the residual gravitational waves also exhibit cross-correlations, the magnitude of which diminishes proportionally to the inverse of the frequency. The prediction is statistically significant and should be verifiable with upcoming gravitational wave detectors that operate at higher frequencies.

A hypothetical supersymmetry framework offers an explanation for why large particles weren't discovered by the Large Hadron Collider; this framework predicts the universe underwent a phase transition around the time of the universe's birth that may create ripples in space time that scientists could detect. If this phase transition happened the way scientists think it did, the universe's conditions may have created tiny particles that make up most of the universe's mass that weren't ripples in space time that scientists could detect.

A reliable and efficient communication system known as semantic communication aims to minimize data transfer and ensure seamless connectivity to diverse users and services. A novel approach to this challenge is presented, incorporating an emergent signaling game framework with a neuro-symbolic artificial intelligence system that facilitates causal reasoning. To design a context-specific communication language, an algorithm is developed to automatically discover linguistic patterns from the data of a targeted network. An innovative neural encoder is then created to encode data using this simplified language, resulting in significantly reduced data transfer. An innovative receiver is also designed that utilizes emergent communication language to reconstruct original message information at the intended destination. Experimental outcomes demonstrate that this proposed Semantic Communication System outperforms conventional solutions in both efficiency and reliability.

The Natural Language Processing area has garnered disproportionate interest from researchers in the past. A primary factor driving this attention lies in the word prediction challenge, where given a sequence of words in a sentence, a model is tasked with recommending the subsequent word. Researchers have addressed this issue through various techniques, combining either syntactic or semantic analysis methods in the past. However, individually, these approaches often fail to yield practical results in real-world applications. For instance, latent semantic analysis can capture semantic text characteristics, yet it disregards syntactic constraints when generating word suggestions. In contrast, more advanced models like Deep Learning integrate both methods to achieve impressive outcomes. While these models can be computationally demanding, hindering their feasibility in certain scenarios, continuous advancements in technology and mathematical modeling enable the development of faster, more accurate systems. A hybrid word suggestion model proposed here, combining elements of Naive Bayes and latent semantic analysis and considering context provided by surrounding words in the sentence, demonstrates considerable promise. Notably, this model achieved a 44.2% accuracy rating in the MSR Sentence Completion Challenge.

Recent advancements in Session-based recommendation systems have gained popularity for providing personalized, real-time suggestions with high recall rates compared to conventional techniques. Recent examples include STAMP and NARM models, which, however, did not perform as expected on Zalando's Fashion-Similar dataset in comparison to a basic collaborative-filtering method. Our proposed strategy targets improving item ranking by leveraging the encoded session information through an attention network and demonstrates the potential through Candidate Rank Embedding in re-ranking. Experimental results demonstrate a considerable enhancement over the baseline on metrics such as Recall, MRR, and Click-Through-Rate in an online setting, and we further observed improvements when combining our method with existing approaches like STAMP and NARM.

We examine a rigid structure composed of two active Brownian particles that share a common center, moving in a 2D environment and driven by activity gradients. We demonstrate that the dynamics of this dimer can be classified into two distinct states: one where the particles move parallel to the gradient, similar to a single active particle, and another where they rotate. The transition between these two states is analyzed, along with the impact of various parameters on this transition, and we find that a dimensionless parameter governing the activity gradients can predict the transition points. Additionally, we explore the presence of stable equilibria and find that the dynamics of the dimer can be understood through a simplified model that identifies three distinct regions corresponding to localized, rotating, and linear movement.

A thorough approach is outlined to model single-phase flow in fractured porous media. The proposed methodology utilizes a discrete fracture model, where fractures are explicitly represented as separate entities within the computational domain. This method enables accurate modeling of the exchange of fluid between the rock and the fractures. It also facilitates the determination of the fractures' widths, which is essential for correctly determining the source of the fluid supplied to the fractures. A rigorous examination is conducted to ensure consistency across different grid refinements, time steps, and flow solvers. A high-resolution, multi-point upstream weighting method is introduced to calculate the fluid flow between the rock and the fractures. This new method outperforms existing techniques in both accuracy and stability. A newly developed non-steady time-weighting method is also introduced to determine the source of the fluid supplied to the fractures. This new method surpasses existing techniques in both accuracy and stability. Several numerical experiments are conducted to validate the proposed approaches and to assess their performance in complex scenarios. One of these experiments involves a numerical replication of the Darcy flow in a 2D setting, which confirms the expected outcomes. Another experiment involves the modeling of single-phase flow with variable fluid properties in a 3D setting, which confirms the expected results. Lastly, a simulation is performed to replicate the steady-state conditions observed in the Raviart-Thomas mixed method.

This study centers on low-energy collision avoidance and maintenance of autonomous drone swarms. Two key issues arise in achieving these goals: firstly, determining optimal strategies to temporarily disband the formation to avoid collisions (collision avoidance reformation), and secondly, effecting this reformation while minimizing the time and energy spent by the drones. To resolve the first challenge, a cellular automata-based method is utilized to identify efficient formations that evade potential collisions. Subsequently, a time- and energy-optimizing control policy is developed to facilitate reformation of these new positions. Notably, a power signal approach is employed to streamline the policy design. Simulation results validate the efficacy of the proposed strategy, demonstrating significant time savings (up to 75%) and reduced energy consumption (up to 50%) compared to previous methods.

This research explores various spectral characteristics of the Seidel matrix associated with a connected chain graph, demonstrating that $-1$ is always an eigenvalue, while other eigenvalues may have a multiplicity of at most two. We derive the multiplicity of the eigenvalue $-1$, the minimum number of unique eigenvalues, eigenvalue limits, the characteristic polynomial, and bounds for the Seidel energy of a chain graph, which outperform previously proposed energy bounds by Haemers. We also obtain the minimum Seidel energy for specific chain graphs of order $n$, along with presenting several unresolved questions.

In our investigation, we focus on a mean-field optimal control issue for stochastic differential equations featuring time-delay, which are solved by fractional Brownian motion with a Hurst parameter exceeding 0.5. Due to the fractional Brownian motion's distinctive properties, encompassing both persistence and non-Markovity, novel approaches need to be applied. Essentially, an appropriate fractional Föllmer-Sorensen process is utilized as a tool to tackle the problem. Utilizing the fractional Föllmer-Sorensen process's specific properties, we derive the HJB equation's relation and the regularity of the value function, which are then followed by the proof of the second-order Taylor expansion of the value function. Ultimately, this enables us to derive the optimal control solution.

We've developed a unique, detailed two-parameter set of finite-band Jacobi elliptic potentials that correspond to the non-self-adjoint Dirac operator, seamlessly linking two well-known limit cases, each associated with the absence or presence of elliptic parameters. To thoroughly analyze the Dirac operator's spectrum, we've made connections between periodic/antiperiodic eigenvalue problems for the Dirac operator with Jacobi elliptic potentials and corresponding Luttinger liquid models, yielding a relationship in the form of a nonlinear matrix eigenvalue problem. This connection allows us to compare the eigenvalue counting function with that of the one-dimensional whole-line Luttinger liquid model, which helps in obtaining minimal and maximal eigenvalue estimates. Additionally, we've obtained detailed local spectral phase transitions information, which becomes self-dual under a specific transformation in the elliptic parameter space. This self-dual structure facilitates the computation of critical values of eigenvalue estimates and phase transition phases, which take on a constant value as the elliptic parameter tends to 0 (purely imaginary parameter). Furthermore, we've obtained direct and indirect methods for counting eigenvalues and phase transitions, which become equivalent under a specific transformation in the elliptic parameter space, providing a broader perspective in the purely imaginary parameter limit.

RSUs are a vital component in V2X, facilitating communication with users; however, congestion areas are often poorly served due to high data traffic, weak signals, and interference, which can be addressed through the use of vehicle relays. To enhance the network in these situations, this research utilizes stochastic geometry to develop an innovative analytical framework for the performance evaluation of vehicular networks incorporating RSUs, vehicle relays, and mobile vehicle users. Our two-dimensional analytical model effectively considers the spatial interdependence of RSUs, vehicle relays, vehicle users, and road infrastructure using a Cox point process. By assuming relay backhaul to RSUs over reserved wireless channels and user association with the closest RSU or relay, we calculate the probability that a typical user is linked to either an RSU or a relay, determine the SIR coverage probability of a typical user, and subsequently, calculate the average effective transmission rate of a typical user within the network. This method enables the quantification of the increase in average effective transmission rate resulting from the deployment of relays.

Wikipedia's ultimate goal is to be an authoritative reference on various topics.  However, due to a limited number of editors, articles that require in-depth knowledge are often hard to find, as Wikipedia's current structure makes it difficult to pinpoint expert-written content.  To address this, we develop a system that identifies articles written at an advanced level, using a Wikipedia-specific dataset, Wikigoogle2008, which consists of 2000 pages. Our system demonstrates accuracy in classifying articles with advanced knowledge, showcasing a 0.75 recall and 0.94 precision, through a 10-fold cross validation.  It appears that articles requiring sophisticated knowledge are relatively rare, as only 6.45% of Wikipedia entries fall into this category.  To facilitate Wikipedia's mission as an authoritative source, we recommend designating a separate section for articles verified by experts, which would improve readers' ability to locate reliable content.

Knowledge distillation is a successful method for accelerating deep neural networks by training a compact model to mimic the behavior of a high-capacity network. Traditionally, this relies on having access to the original network's training data and parameters, which isn't always feasible due to storage or privacy constraints in real-world applications. This study introduces decision-based black-box knowledge distillation, allowing a model to be trained on the behavior of a network whose internal workings are inaccessible, as long as it produces classification outputs. When access to the original data is possible, a training sample's resistance to other classes is quantified by measuring the distance between its class and the network's decision boundaries, which is used to assign a soft label to the sample. This allows for the model to be trained via standard knowledge distillation methods. When access to the original data isn't possible, pseudo-samples are created based on the network's decision boundaries and assigned soft labels, which serve as a transfer set for training the model. Our proposed approach is evaluated on multiple networks and datasets and shows positive results. Code is available at: https://github.com/zwang84/zsdb3kd.

Researchers have observed the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ decay mode for the first time, and have also gathered evidence for the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S$ decay mode, utilizing a 3.0 $\text{fb}^{-1}$ dataset of $pp$ collisions collected at 7 and 8 TeV center-of-mass energies by the LHCb. The branching fractions for these decays are calculated as follows: The $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 \bar{K}^0$ branching fraction is estimated at (4.3±0.5±0.3±0.3±0.6) ×10^-4, and the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} \bar{K}^0$ branching fraction is estimated at (2.8±0.3±0.2±0.2±0.4) ×10^-4, with the given uncertainties stemming from various sources.

The $C^*$-algebra formalism of topological T-duality developed by Mathai and Rosenberg is applied to a broad class of topological spaces encompassing torus bundles, nilmanifolds, and other examples from string theory. By constructing T-duals from commutative $C^*$-algebras representing string backgrounds, we establish a general framework for classifying string backgrounds. Our method is essentially universal, universally invariant, and illustrates the string background's topological characteristics. A non-commutative $C^*$-algebra example of non-commutative T-duality is presented. Additionally, the almost abelian solvmanifolds, a subclass of solvmanifolds with abelian derived lie algebra, are found to satisfy the requirements for topological T-duality. By constructing the duals of specific algebras corresponding to the $3$-manifolds of Wolczek and $\mathbb{R}^2$ bent tori, we provide concrete examples of non-commutative duality.

Reinforcement learning efficiency can be significantly enhanced through imitation learning by leveraging expert guidance. However, relying on expert demonstrations is often impractical or too costly due to the high expense of gathering them. In this research, we introduce CoImitate - a novel algorithm within the Imitation learning framework. CoImitate leverages cooperative game theory to develop strategies where agents can learn each other's policies without needing expert demonstrations. By formulating a potential maximization problem using each agent's policy derivative estimates and applying the Fenchel-Anderson gradient Ascent algorithm, CoImitate achieves steady-state convergence where the agents' policies maximize the potential. Furthermore, we prove that in the long run, agents' policies converge to maximizing the potential, an indicator of optimality. We also present numerical experiments validating the theoretical findings.

This paper proposes a metric function that yields an optimal performance on average, which significantly reduces decoding computations while maintaining superior error-correction performance for polarization-adjusted convolutional codes. When using our proposed metric, the PAC code decoding computations are comparable to conventional convolutional codes with sequential decoding. Moreover, our results demonstrate improved error-correction performance for low-rate PAC codes with the proposed metric. We show that using the polarized cutoff rate as the bias in our metric function reduces the risk of incorrect path selection during decoding, exponentially decreasing as the incorrect path depth increases. We also prove and validate the Pareto distribution of PAC code computation complexity. Additionally, we provide a scaling-bias procedure, which allows the risk of incorrect path selection to be quantified and makes the PAC code decoding computations more stable and predictable.

This project tackles the complex problem of simultaneously monitoring the positions and shapes of hands and objects in a sequence of depth point cloud data, starting from the known poses in the initial frame. To achieve this, we introduce a network called HandTrackNet, the first point cloud-based hand joint tracking system, to calculate hand joint movement between frames. Our novel hand pose canonicalization module simplifies this task and enables accurate tracking of hand joints. By converting these joints into a template-based hand model called MANO, our system can reconstruct the entire hand. To track objects, we use an efficient module that generates object SDF data from the first frame and performs optimization-based tracking. Our system can then generate object joints by applying the generated SDF to a template mesh. Looking ahead, our system has the potential to track sophisticated grasping scenes and a range of human hand-object interactions.

This study presents a theoretical investigation into Coxeter groups of rank 4 using Poincaré polynomial research as the primary tool. A comprehensive analysis of these groups is conducted based on their star diagrams and related properties. Additionally, the abstract conjecture regarding Coxeter groups of rank 4 is verified.

A novel, markerless extrinsic calibration system is introduced that relies on real-world depth camera data rather than simulation or fiducial markers. Our system leverages machine learning to automatically develop and utilize real-world models for identifying and positioning the end-effector, predicting object rotation, and pinpointing critical points in a single image frame. A mathematical transformation and a keypoint-matching algorithm allow us to accurately estimate end-effector pose based on rotation and keypoint data. Enhanced by a smoothing algorithm, the estimated end-effector pose is optimized for precision and performance. Furthermore, our system's capacity for real-time calibration without manual intervention enables seamless integration with various practical applications. A 20 mm error margin for end-effector pose positioning was achieved through extensive testing.

This research develops a model for identifying treatment interference that draws on graph theory, focusing on direct and indirect influences. Direct influence is viewed as direct edge connection between treatment nodes, whereas indirect influence is seen as shared nodes among treatments. Both forms of interference are considered in the model's development. A statistical method is proposed for estimating the standard treatment effect, accounting for both direct and indirect interference. The method involves leveraging shared features among treatments to adjust the model. Extensive simulations demonstrate the efficacy of this approach in reducing bias, which correlates with the degree of shared nodes. Furthermore, practical applications of this method are examined in disease network construction and multiple treatment scenarios.

Calculations of neutrino emissions from self-destructing dark matter particles within a star are being conducted. In the core of a star that has not yet undergone nuclear reactions, it's observed that the interactions between these particles and the star's constituent atoms via a particular particle can produce an unusually high number of neutrinos, which may equal and potentially surpass those produced by the star's nuclear reactions early on. This process primarily involves two reactions: a collision of two dark matter particles resulting in neutrinos or intermediate particles that then decay into neutrinos, which may be produced in large quantities due to the high concentration of these particles in a star, potentially exceeding those of more standard particle physics-based methods.

The ongoing UNIONS project, the most comprehensive optical survey to date in the Northern sky, has partnered with CFIS for $r$-band data collection, boasting exceptional seeing of 0.65 arcseconds and complete magnitude 24.5 for precise weak-lensing research. Our analysis covers an expansive 1700 square degrees of the sky, cataloging 40 million galaxies, translating to a density of 6.8 per square arcminute. A shear bias analysis was conducted on each night's data using fringes, confirming previous knowledge that there's an average shear bias of 0.004 and a residual multiplicative shear bias of -0.013 across all data. However, the presence of fringes significantly reduces the shear bias to near zero. Building upon the base shear catalog, we applied a technique to remove systematics based on galaxy colors, eliminating any remaining color-dependent bias. With this thorough research, we generated a final shear catalog, verifying the findings using simulations and comparing them to those from the KiDS-1000 survey. The research also demonstrates that the remaining systematic impact is minimal, at most 8 percent. The final catalog is accessible through the COSMOS Legacy Archive, and the research, as well as the catalog, will be used for future weak-lensing studies.

A notable consequence of a finding made by Veech more than 50 years ago, relating to the mod $2$ form of the Kronecker-Weyl theorem, has to do with sequences of irrational rotations of the form $T_{\alpha,p}(x) = \alpha x + p$, where $\alpha$ is a real number irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$ and $0 \leq x < 1$, which translates to the parity of cardinalities being evenly distributed among sets defined by $0 < x < 1$ and $0 \leq x < 1$ respectively. In this paper, a broader view of this phenomenon is offered, which also reveals an unexpected connection to Scaramucci's equation, a well-known problem in number theory.

We prove that for k-rational singularities of local complete intersections, k-Du Bois classification applies. For hypersurfaces, k-rationality can be determined based on the minimal exponent. Moreover, certain local vanishing properties for k-rational and k-Du Bois singularities have been identified. These properties were also discovered separately by [FL2].

We've observed the appearance of field-induced Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless correlations in a weakly coupled, spin-1/2 Heisenberg material called [Cu(pz)2(2-HOpy)2](PF6)2. Due to its moderate exchange coupling of about 6.8 Kelvin, the application of laboratory magnetic fields produces a noticeable anisotropy of the spin correlations in an XY plane. This significant BKT regime develops because of a weak interlayer exchange of about one millikelvin that causes 3D correlations as the critical temperature is approached, resulting in an exponential increase in spin-correlation length. Nuclear magnetic resonance, muon spin resonance measurements and quantum Monte Carlo simulations using the experimentally determined parameters are employed to determine the critical temperatures associated with BKT transitions as well as long-range order. Finite-size scaling of the spin stiffness based on our in-plane theory shows a perfect match between theoretical and experimental critical temperatures, clearly indicating that the complex magnetic phase diagram of [Cu(pz)2(2-HOpy)2](PF6)2 is determined by field-induced XY anisotropy and concomitant BKT physics.

Adding three right-handed neutrinos and a simple QCD axion sector to the Standard Model effectively explains multiple phenomena including neutrino oscillations, dark matter, and baryon asymmetry. In doing so, it also resolves issues with strong CP problems and stabilizes the electroweak vacuum while fitting within observational limits of Higgs inflation. The model, referred to as $a\nu$MSM, undergoes a detailed analysis to examine the nature of dark matter within this framework. The presence of an inflection point within Higgs inflation is found not to significantly impact dark matter composition, and thus the model's implications for dark matter production are primarily investigated through the parameter space where the curvaton mechanism is relevant. The model is found to satisfy LHC and future direct detection facility constraints while being consistent with observational limits of dark matter abundance. In a specific sector of the model's parameter space, its implications for LHC searches and future direct detection experiments are explored, particularly in the context of resonant production of the lightest neutrino species via a narrow resonance. The model is found to be distinct from a scenario involving the simple Sterile Neutrino model in this context.

This study optimizes the execution time of the ABW protocol by minimizing the number of Clifford gates needed to prepare a magic state with a specific amount of magic, thereby enhancing the efficiency of the protocol in a quantum simulation environment. By developing a novel method to determine the minimum number of Clifford gates required to generate a certain amount of magic, the study refines the existing bound and finds that the number of gates needed is less than the total number of magic states used, multiplied by the number of copies. This finding surpasses the current best-known bound and is proven to be close to the best possible bound, with the gap being proportional to the number of magic states. Additionally, the study finds that the proven bound is close to the best-known lower bound, which is determined by the least amount of magic in any individual state. Specifically, the study finds that at least half of the magic states used must remain unpolarized, and that optimizing the proven bound is statistically unlikely.

This research employs the Tsallis holographic dark energy model in two scenarios, 
non-interacting and interacting, to calculate essential parameters for the energy 
density equation of state within the FRW universe, analogous to a quintessence model.
We will reassess the evolution paths of these models by creating phase diagrams, 
where the real universe's paths are isolated based on energy density requirements.
We'll compare these diagrams to standard quintessence results, highlighting 
substitutive quintessence characteristics.
Additionally, we'll analyze fine-tuning in these models through parameter space 
examination, estimating the volume where the fractional energy density exceeds one.
We'll further discuss a potential transition from the interacting and non-interacting 
TCDHE scenarios, marking a distinction between these models.
This work sets the stage for exploring interactions in quintessence models, where 
the fractional energy density may exceed one, contradicting real universe conditions.

Between October 2019 and April 2020, the LAMOST performed a unique observational study using 39 nights to monitor low-resolution spectra at wavelengths ranging from 3670 to 4280 Angstroms, capturing 9289 target stars' variability. This study, which was designed to identify main-sequence stars exhibiting lithium emissions, analyzed a total of 884,610 spectra segments, with the majority having a signal-to-noise ratio exceeding 10. To analyze the variability, LAMOST employed a combination of methods, including lithium line shape measurements, spectral feature comparisons, and periodicity analyses. To pinpoint periodic stars, LAMOST employed an automated algorithm to identify patterns in the data, which were then visually verified by researchers. This observation sought out lithium emission stars primarily using a semi-automated approach and also discovered other periodic stars in the process, yielding a total of 8832 low-periodic objects, 934 binary stars, and  among these,  different types including  gamma Doradus,  delta Scuti, and variable stars in the magnitude range of 9-12.  This is a preliminary stage and the final results have yet to be optimized or refined.

Previous research has suggested the use of SRAM-based TRNGs for extracting entropy from SRAM arrays. As these arrays are commonly employed in specialized or general-purpose chips for storing program data and instructions, SRAM-based TRNGs offer an attractive alternative to dedicated hardware TRNGs for its simplicity and efficacy. Nevertheless, existing SRAM-based TRNGs suffer from reduced throughput and prolonged generation times, necessitating the proposal of a new and enhanced design. Our proposed SRAM-based TRNG can be integrated within a configurable SOC, operating in three distinct modes: a high-speed mode of 200 MSps, a low-power mode of 14.1 kbps, and an intermediate mode of 445.5 kbps. Furthermore, it offers an enhanced generation time of 5.56 ns and 2.82 ns in the high-speed and low-speed modes, respectively. Additionally, its hardware complexity is minimized, with only a single TWOTIA and one MTCMOS transistor required. By utilizing the entropy-extraction capability of the TWOTIA and incorporating a binary counter for downscaling the clock, we have developed a highly efficient SRNG that can efficiently utilize the entropy contained within a standard SRAM array.

A preliminary design and simulation of a single-electron resistive switch has been developed, incorporating two linear molecules that interact electrostatically: one molecule is a single-electron transistor and the other is a single-electron trap. To confirm our design's validity, a theoretical analysis was performed, integrating density functional theory and non-equilibrium Green's functions to evaluate the electronic properties of these molecular assemblies under 1.0 V. The outcomes demonstrate that a switch with high on-off ratios can be achieved, even when the length of the assemblies doesn't meet the single-electron fluctuation criterion. Additionally, a new type of single-electron trap was identified, utilizing a charged electron in an anti-bonding molecular orbital, which significantly amplifies its spatial extent. This novel single-electron trap is found to maintain resistance ratios exceeding 10 for structures smaller than 10 nm in length, reducing energy losses and significantly minimizing single-electron trap radiation.

The concept of loop-tree duality has emerged as a promising approach for numerically computing complex multi-loop scattering amplitudes, offering an attractive alternative to conventional methods. By applying loop-tree duality, the Feynman integrands are simplified to a form that only captures physical information, resulting in a causal representation. In this study, we explore the causal representation's potential to contribute to our understanding of scattering processes. By examining the underlying field configurations that contribute to the amplitude, we can investigate the role of boundary conditions and the appearance of loop effects, which can be used to clarify the loop-tree duality's physical implications. Our analysis suggests that self-interactions introduce an asymmetry in the scattering process, affecting the asymptotic regions. Furthermore, we find that the causal representation can be represented by a network of interactions that are both spatially extended and temporally extended. In the case of two-loopscattering processes, the representations exhibit a level of complexity that is comparable to the Feynman representation in terms of the number of terms. In the asymptotic future or past, the Feynman representation becomes dominant, whereas the causal representation gains significance in the asymptotic intermediate regions. In the case of two-loopscattering processes, the amplitude's self-interacting component exhibits a distinct behavior in the asymptotic regions, where the planar and non-planar loop topologies display contrasting results.

This paper aims to provide a direct and straightforward proof of eigenfunction expansion formulas for one-dimensional quantum walks with two possible states, similar to classical Fourier series representations. In addition, we will derive a minimum core property for these quantum walks, analogous to the Heisenberg uncertainty principle.

This study examines the composition of hybrid stars formed by neutrons, protons, and various other particles. The analysis combines the Sigma-omega-rho model for a specific nuclear phase with two distinct quark phase models, and incorporates Maxwell and Gibbs conditions to understand the phase transition. By analyzing mass-radius relations, a hybrid star's mass is predicted to be limited to twice the mass of the sun.

The introduction of $q$-deformation into optomechanical systems reveals opportunities to amplify non-traditional optical phenomena. This insight drives an investigation of the optical behavior within a linearly coupled $q$-deformed optomechanical system. Composed of two deformed cavities interacting with mechanical mirrors and coupled through a transmission matrix, this system's behavior can be contrasted with that of its optomechanical analog. As a result, the optical phenomena, including amplification and absorption, are found to be intensified in the optomechanical system. Furthermore, the effects of $q$-deformation reveal the possibility of modifying phase transitions and amplifying optical shifts. In addition, the analysis reveals dual solutions associated with optomechanical instability, an occurrence not present in the optomechanical system. This research provides a theoretical framework for utilizing $q$-deformation to control and understand optomechanical interactions.

In a previous study, I developed a model where the classical bodies of a rigid dumbbell could be represented by two negative scissors states, exhibiting closed trajectories. This was based on a specific assumption regarding the bodies' Liouville theorem. This paper explores potential violations of that assumption and describes scenarios in which the bodies' trajectories may become complex. To investigate this further, a simplified model of a dumbbell was used, where the bodies' motion was governed by two simple dynamical systems. A surprising outcome of this study was that the trajectories of the dumbbell's components could either remain simple or complex, with this state transition often occurring abruptly. Furthermore, it was observed that when the dumbbell's state transitioned from complex to simple, the relative orbit of its components undergoes a resonance transition, specifically from being wild to being regular.

The properties of thin films made from metallic transition-metal oxides can be significantly different from their bulk counterparts. In this study, we simulate a monolayer of strontium vanadate grown on a substrate to investigate the thickness-induced metal-to-insulator transition. We found that two different terminations lead to the same insulating behavior at equilibrium but exhibit distinct behavior when doped or subjected to a gate voltage. Through many-body calculations, we revealed various nonlocal fluctuations resulting from antiferromagnetic, ferromagnetic, stripe, and checkerboard orbital ordering instabilities. By considering the role of orbital degrees of freedom, we explain how these instabilities emerge and demonstrate how ultra-thin film reconstruction and changes to coordination polyhedra result in unique material properties.

The occurrence of diffusion can be seen across various natural phenomena, and this widespread application is attributed to the broad implications of the central limit theorem. In the past, scientists discovered an extension of typical dynamics, resulting in "anomalous" diffusion that accounts for distributions characterized by long, power-law tails. One such physical system - laser-cooled atomic ensembles - offers an optimal platform to study such phenomena, primarily due to its distinctive friction force. This interplay between laser cooling and anomalous dynamics is likely to reveal profound and predictive insights into both equilibrium and non-equilibrium statistical physics. In experiments involving cold-atom systems, scientists can manipulate and adjust various system parameters to observe changes in the system's behavior, and this has been achieved by analyzing non-normalized states associated with rare events, utilizing tools derived from infinite ergodic theory, resulting in new findings.

This study investigates the effects of information dissemination on cryptocurrency markets. Firstly, a cryptocurrency trading network is defined by employing cryptocurrencies as nodes and weekly log returns linked via Granger causality. The analysis traces its development over time, focusing on years 2020 and 2021. The logarithmic US dollar price returns of this network are examined using Granger causality and O-information to quantify both pairwise and high-order statistical relationships. The Granger causality results indicate peaks in significant events, while the corresponding network structure exhibits stability, with most influential nodes being cryptocurrencies. Contrasting with pairwise analysis, stable coins appear in few synergistic connections, but when considering high-order relationships, they dominate synergistic circuits, highlighting their role in higher-order effects. Furthermore, a high volume of total transactions in US dollars in the first semester of 2021 triggered a shift in the cryptocurrency network towards increased complexity. The study demonstrates that both pairwise and high-order approaches to financial systems offer valuable insights into cryptocurrency behavior.

The formation of particles from trace gases is a crucial source of cloud condensation nuclei that facilitate the creation of clouds due to their role in overcoming extremely high supersaturated conditions needed for homogeneous water droplet formation. The application of quantum chemistry in modeling this process has become more accurate with advancements in pathway calculations involving large quantum chemical packages. The template approach allows faster simulations at the quantum chemical molecular mechanics hybrid level using density functional theory templates but has primarily been utilized for gas-phase reactions. This study presents the extension of the template methodology to solution-phase reactions relevant to aerosol particle formation. To model this, a hybrid quantum chemical molecular mechanics framework is employed to calculate the ground state and optimized structures of the system, followed by an orbital-based calculation of the system's energy. The study demonstrates the efficacy of the template approach in modeling particle formation via homogeneous nucleation and shows a positive correlation between the calculated and experimental lattice energies.

We establish the definitions for a compact perception pair, compactifying a perception pair, and compactifying a space of operators invariant under group actions and non-expansive in nature. It's proven that every perception pair with measurements from a totally bounded space and rich enough to impose a metric on their common domain, becomes a compact perception pair when equipped with a specific topology. Furthermore, it's shown that the set of non-expansive group invariant operators can be compactified using a specific kernel, and that the fixed point space of a contraction mapping on a measurement space can be compactified when the contraction is group invariant.

The way solids respond to temperature gradients can be understood by applying the concept of transverse energy currents, which vary based on gravitational potential. In order to simplify this concept, we develop a model that represents transverse energy currents as the difference between two average energy flows along specific directions. The transverse energy current is represented by an equation that considers variations in gravitational potential, and this effect can be significant in certain situations. The importance of considering orientation-dependent transport coefficients, especially those related to transport of heat, is also stressed. To validate our model, we examine the transverse energy current in superfluid helium and compare it with existing research findings. Furthermore, we discuss potential applications and experimental approaches to investigate the transverse energy current in solid materials.

In various machine learning scenarios, simpler models are generally preferred to their more complex counterparts, and controlling model complexity is a major objective for several methods, such as regularization, hyperparameter optimization, and architecture planning. For deep learning models, understanding how complexity is controlled has been a challenging task, given that many conventional methods are unsuitable for their inherent complexity. Our research introduces a concept called geometric complexity, quantifying the variability of model functions using a discrete Dirichlet energy metric. By combining theoretical analysis with empirical evidence, we demonstrate that several widespread training heuristics, such as parameter and spectral regularization, as well as parameter initialization techniques, serve to control geometric complexity.

A new approach for directly extracting the Wilson coefficients of rare $b\to s$ processes is developed using $B^0\to K^{*0}\mu^+\mu^-$ decays within an unbinned maximum likelihood framework. This novel method outperforms traditional Wilson coefficient determination by utilizing all available data and accounting for experimental correlations without segmentation into $q^2$ bins. Simulation results confirm the improved sensitivity and potential to leverage the complete Run 1 and 2 LHCb dataset in practice.

Automated essay grading has been a persistent challenge in Natural Language Processing.  Despite years of research, it remains an only partially resolved issue, with notable variations in performance depending on the specific task and dataset used for training.  In this study, we examine the effectiveness of recent pre-trained transformer models such as BERT and RoBERTa in automated essay grading, and also investigate whether combining multiple models can lead to improved results.  Our analysis is conducted using the APEC14 dataset, which allows us to compare our findings to those of a recent survey on state-of-the-art methods for automated essay grading.  Our main contributions are the development of a custom dataset preparation pipeline and the creation of a GitHub repository that includes all necessary code and configuration files for reproducing our results.

Given a simplicial complex defining a tensor's marginalizations, we restrict them to rank one, an idea developed from Kirkup and Sullivant's work on toric models. We delve into the toric ideals arising from such marginal independence models, with a specific focus on models for random graphs and matroids' independent set polytopes. We also explore numerical methods for parameter estimation through both Euclidean distance and maximum likelihood techniques and establish a database for small model examples.

A higher education system or similar opportunities can drive social mobility across generations by allowing individuals to rise above their family's economic status. To examine this dynamic in societies with social mobility limitations, a new model allocates opportunities to maximize the benefits they provide to current and future generations. Our model reveals that, in order to maximize long-term payoffs, it's beneficial to give priority to lower socioeconomically situated individuals who have greater potential to rise to better socioeconomical standings. The result can lead to socioeconomic affirmative action. The duration and intensity of this practice vary depending on specific conditions. The proposed model also offers avenues for exploring more intricate relationships between different socioeconomical groups in various societal settings.

The symmetry of wavefunctions under parity for particles of arbitrary spin is responsible for determining the wavefunction exchange statistics when the particles are permuted. According to non-relativistic quantum mechanics, the properties of angular momentum alone account for the sign factor resulting from the particle permutation, which relates spin to particle exchange statistics in this context.

We introduce an upgraded RingCT protocol that supports stealth addresses in conjunction with Delegated Proof of Stake, resulting in Delegated RingCT.
The Delegated RingCT scheme is comprised of an integrated signature and encryption framework, combining a public key encryption protocol and two types of signatures along with linkable ring signatures, alongside non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs.
A comprehensive description of Delegated RingCT, along with security evidence and an implementation, is presented.
To evaluate Delegated RingCT in a practical setting, we modify NTBSCDT, a decentralized cryptocurrency, to incorporate the new protocol.
Our experimental outcomes demonstrate that Delegated RingCT and NTBSCDT exhibit high levels of security and scalability.

If more specific subclasses of linear systems can be solved in near-logarithmic space, this capability can be applied to solve a broader range of linear systems within a similar space complexity. Our findings build on work by Kyng and Zhang who previously made similar discoveries in terms of time complexity, utilizing reductions between approximate solvers; our own proof demonstrates that these reductions can be implemented using threshold circuits with specific characteristics.

Researchers have made the initial detection of three massive gauge bosons simultaneously produced in high-energy collisions between protons.  These collisions were performed at the CERN LHC with the CMS experiment's data set that contains 137 fb$^{-1}$ worth of information.  Separate searches for individual combinations of bosons, including W boson variations, have been done using several different patterns of final particle arrangements.  Together, the signals for these processes indicate a cross-section of boson creation that is slightly larger than that of the standard model at a 95% confidence level, with significant variations in intensity expected to continue growing as more data becomes available.  Additionally, the data has given insight into how these particles interact when they are highly energetic, as well as how they decay when they are no longer in their ground state.

Previous foundational Hebrew NLP tasks have heavily relied on the 30-year-old Hebrew Treebank. This outdated single-source corpus lacks the diversity of modern Hebrew, found primarily on the web. This research paper addresses this issue by presenting a new, open-access UD Hebrew treebank. This corpus, created by sampling various topics from Hebrew Wikipedia, provides a much-needed upgrade to NLP's understanding of contemporary Hebrew. The project evaluates its own annotations, validates results using automated tools, and achieves new state-of-the-art results on UD NLP tasks by combining advanced language models with innovative approaches. Additionally, the project updates and releases the existing UD HTB annotation scheme, incorporating the improvements from the new Hebrew corpus.
